If $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is integrable and continuous, then for every $t\in\mathbb
R$ the function $b\mapsto\int_{(-\infty,b]} f(x)\,dx$ has derivative $f(t)$ at $b=t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a quantile conditional integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_quantile_conditional_integral}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_quantile_conditional_integral}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_integral_Iic, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_Iic_standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.continuous_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.continuous_standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianQuantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R$, let $\Phi$ be its distribution
function, and let $Q$ be the total Gaussian quantile. For $\rho,t,d,a\in\mathbb R$ with
$a\in(0,1)$, the function $p\mapsto\int_{(-\infty,Q(p)]}\Phi\bigl((t-\rho
x)/d\bigr)\,d\gamma(x)$ is differentiable at $a$, with derivative $\Phi\bigl((t-\rho
Q(a))/d\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of a Gaussian CDF composition]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianBivariateSlope_right}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianBivariateSlope_right}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianIsoperimetric, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hasDerivAt_standardGaussianQuantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho,a\in\mathbb R$ and $b\in(0,1)$. The function
\[
p\longmapsto \Phi\!\left(\frac{Q(p)-\rho Q(a)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}\right)
\]
has derivative at $p=b$ equal to
\[
\frac{\varphi\!\left(\frac{Q(b)-\rho
Q(a)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}\right)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,U(b)},
\]
where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function, $Q$ is its lower quantile,
$\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density, and $U(b)=\varphi(Q(b))$ is the Gaussian
isoperimetric profile.
\end{lemma}

Let $\rho\in(-1,1)$ and $a,b\in(0,1)$. As a function of its second threshold, the
Gaussian bivariate stability at thresholds $a$ and $b$ has derivative at $b$ equal to
\[
\Phi\!\left(\frac{Q(a)-\rho Q(b)}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}\right),
\]
where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function and $Q$ is its lower
quantile.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concavity of bivariate Gaussian stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.concaveOn_gaussianBivariateStability_left}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.concaveOn_gaussianBivariateStability_left}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho,b\in(0,1)$. For $a\in[0,1]$, consider the probability that a pair of
independent standard Gaussian random variables $(Z_1,Z_2)$ satisfies $\Phi(Z_1)\le a$
and $\Phi\!\left(\rho Z_1+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Z_2\right)\le b$, where $\Phi$ is the standard
Gaussian distribution function. As a function of $a$, this probability is concave on
$[0,1]$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $0<\rho<1$ and $a,b\in[0,1]$. If $(X,Y)$ is a pair of real random variables with
joint law equal to the product of two standard Gaussian measures, then the probability
that $\Phi(X)\le a$ and $\Phi(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)\le b$ is at least $ab$, where
$\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetry of correlated Gaussian densities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianPDF_correlated_symmetry}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianPDF_correlated_symmetry}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho,s,a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $s\ne0$ and $s^2=1-\rho^2$. For the standard
Gaussian density $\varphi$, $\varphi((b-\rho a)/s)\varphi(a)=\varphi((a-\rho
b)/s)\varphi(b)$.
\end{lemma}
